definitions.explanation: The position of lying with one's face and front of body facing downward.

examples.japanese: {俯|うつぶ}せ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{寝|ね}る→寝る：00470_neru⟧。
⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{俯|うつぶ}せ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いけない→いけない：02335_ikenai⟧。
examples.english: You must not put a baby face down.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{床|ゆか}→床：03652_yuka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{俯|うつぶ}せ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なって→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦{倒|たお}れて→倒れる：01160_taoreru⟧⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: He was lying face down on the floor.

notes:
{俯|うつぶ}せ describes the prone position — lying with the face and body facing downward. It contrasts with ⟦{仰向|あおむ}け→仰向け：05548_aomuke⟧ (face up, supine).

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {俯|うつぶ}せ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to lie face down
- {俯|うつぶ}せ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{寝|ね}る→寝る：00470_neru⟧: to sleep on one's stomach
- {俯|うつぶ}せ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{姿勢|しせい}→姿勢：00371_shisei⟧: prone position
- {俯|うつぶ}せ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{倒|たお}れる→倒れる：01160_taoreru⟧: to fall face down

USAGE:
Appears in everyday body position descriptions, medical contexts (sleeping posture advice for infants), exercise instructions, and narrative scenes. Note that sleeping face down ({俯|うつぶ}せ⟦{寝|ね}→寝る：00470_neru⟧) is often discussed in health advice as a habit to avoid.

WRITING:
The kanji {俯|うつぶ} is relatively uncommon; this word is frequently written in hiragana as うつぶせ or うつ{伏|ぶ}せ.
